title: Jonah and the Extraction
premise: Jonah Vane, a transport-safety investigator haunted by the crash that killed his wife and daughter in row twelve, receives a calendar invitation from his handler — dead for three days — summoning him to a meeting already in progress. Pulled into a conspiracy inside the very agency that rewrote the rules he lives by, Jonah discovers a planned attack designed to look like an accident, timed to exploit the border checkpoint shift change when oversight goes dark. As the corrupt director who buried the original crash report closes in, Jonah must choose between the survival protocols that have kept him alive and the truth that could destroy everything he's become. In the end, Jonah exposes the plot at the checkpoint itself, sacrificing his fabricated identity to save strangers in row twelve of another plane — and finally grieves the family he never allowed himself to mourn.
about_author: Tamsin Eriksen is a former aviation safety analyst who left the industry after a decade of investigating incidents no one wanted explained. She writes thrillers from a coastal town where she keeps a running list of accidents officially ruled 'unremarkable.'

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Five years after the crash, Jonah works crash sites by the book, cataloging wreckage with clinical detachment. A routine inspection at a regional airfield turns strange: debris patterns don't match the official cause. Emotional beat: grief held at arm's length begins to crack.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. His handler Marsh — dead three days per the obituary — sends a calendar invite for tomorrow, 0600, Terminal C. The attachment contains Jonah's own personnel file, redacted in ways only insiders would understand. Emotional beat: dread sharpened into purpose; the rules have changed again.

chapters.title: Terminal C, 0600
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. He attends the meeting and finds it mid-session: six strangers, one empty chair, and a briefing about an attack disguised as an accident. Security storms the room; the group scatters. Jonah escapes with a stolen drive. Emotional beat: paranoia becomes certainty.

chapters.title: The Empty Chair
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa Renner, one of the six attendees and a disgraced air-traffic auditor. She tracks Jonah down, convinced the empty chair belonged to Marsh and that Jonah is either bait or a traitor. Uneasy alliance forms. Emotional beat: distrust as a survival instinct.

chapters.title: Redactions
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Decoding the drive, Jonah finds the original report from his family's crash — altered before he ever read it. The same signature approved both versions: Director Callum Reeve. Emotional beat: the floor drops out of five years of controlled mourning.

chapters.title: Shift Change
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. She explains the window: border checkpoint shift changes create a ninety-minute oversight gap, the perfect cover for the staged accident. They map likely targets. Emotional beat: the abstract threat acquires a clock.

chapters.title: What the Rules Are For
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Flashback interwoven with present: how Marsh taught him that procedure is armor against corruption. Now Jonah must break protocol to follow the evidence. He contacts a records clerk off-book. Emotional beat: loyalty to the dead versus loyalty to the living.

chapters.title: The Clerk
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. The clerk agrees to pull maintenance logs, then vanishes overnight; her apartment shows signs of a tidy, professional search. Jonah realizes they're being hunted by people who clean up cleanly. Emotional beat: guilt over another casualty in row twelve's long shadow.

chapters.title: Reeve
chapters.summary: POV Callum Reeve. The antagonist's chapter: his philosophy of necessary fictions, his role in rewriting the old report, and his order to close the Jonah problem permanently. Emotional beat: chilling conviction — power justified as protection.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Hiding in a decommissioned control tower, she and Jonah calculate odds: expose Reeve through channels (slow, compromised) or intercept the attack directly (dangerous, illegal). Jonah chooses interception. Emotional beat: the price of survival named aloud.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Using Marsh's dead-man credentials, Jonah infiltrates the agency's scheduling system and finds the planted flight manifest — a charter routed through the checkpoint gap, overloaded manifests falsified to guarantee catastrophe. Emotional beat: cold clarity of purpose.

chapters.title: The Mole
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Someone inside their circle feeds Reeve their location; the tower is raided. Ilsa covers Jonah's escape and is taken. Emotional beat: betrayal, and the terrible math of who gets saved.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Reeve personally questions her, offering reinstatement for silence. She stalls, learns the attack timeline has moved up twelve hours. Emotional beat: defiance under pressure; power's corruption shown face-to-face.

chapters.title: Dead Man's Hand
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Grieving and alone, Jonah discovers a hidden message from Marsh — the handler faked his death to finish this, and left a key: physical evidence of Reeve's alterations, stored where it all began, at the original crash site. Emotional beat: inheritance of a mission.

chapters.title: Wreckage Field
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. At the memorialized crash site, now a fenced field, Jonah retrieves the evidence while evading surveillance — and stands, for the first time, where row twelve came to rest. Emotional beat: grief finally entered instead of bypassed.

chapters.title: Twelve Hours Early
chapters.summary: POV alternating Jonah/Ilsa. The attack is moved up; the checkpoint gap opens at dawn. Jonah trades the evidence to a sympathetic insider for Ilsa's release, splitting his assets between justice and rescue. Emotional beat: sacrifice as strategy.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Nine
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Dawn at Checkpoint Nine. Jonah gets himself detained deliberately to be inside the system during the gap, planting the evidence into the incoming shift's review queue so it cannot be quietly deleted. Emotional beat: turning the machine's own rules against it.

chapters.title: Ninety Minutes
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Freed but racing, Ilsa reaches the charter's ground crew and grounds the flight through a legitimate safety violation — using the rulebook Reeve corrupted as a weapon. Emotional beat: procedure redeemed.

chapters.title: The Accident That Didn't Happen
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Reeve confronts Jonah in the checkpoint office as the flight sits grounded, the plot collapsing. A tense standoff ends when the new shift arrives and finds the evidence queue blinking. Reeve walks — for now. Emotional beat: victory with a bitter aftertaste.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Weeks later, an independent inquiry convenes. Ilsa testifies; the clerk's recovered logs surface; Reeve's network unravels outward. Jonah watches from the gallery, anonymous. Emotional beat: accountability arriving slowly, imperfectly, but arriving.

chapters.title: Names Read Aloud
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. At the fifth-anniversary memorial, the victims' names are read including row twelve. Jonah speaks his family's names publicly for the first time, shedding the identity survival built for him. Emotional beat: mourning completed, identity reclaimed.

chapters.title: Tomorrow, 0600
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. A new calendar invitation arrives — from Marsh's account, still active. Jonah smiles, packs the drive, and books a flight. Some meetings you attend; some you call. Emotional beat: forward motion — vigilance chosen freely, not imposed by fear.
